teaser.text: BYD Company Limited is a Chinese manufacturer whose main business is selling electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, supported by batteries, components and factories it largely controls. A dollar enters when an outside customer buys a finished vehicle, battery, electronic product or project, and leaves through materials, people, factories, delivery, support, financing and tax.

blocks.heading: Where could BYD's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted price is HKD97.03 in October 2027, a 33% total return including dividends. It rises to HKD122.44 in October 2028, a 69% return. By October 2029, it reaches HKD156.72, a 117% return.

BYD’s weighted forecast reaches HKD97.03 in October 2027 if overseas growth becomes profitable, earnings recover and cash generation returns. That outcome implies a +33% return including dividends. blocks.heading: What has to go right for BYD's forecast?

paragraphs.text: EBITDA is the main operating swing. The base row starts at CNY140,833m and reaches CNY171,875m. The analyst compilation expects net profit of CNY38,873m and CNY49,310.65m in its next two forecast years, supporting a recovery. The bear row starts at CNY110,083m and ends at CNY116,750m because recent operating income fell and the latest half-year remained weaker. The bull row starts at CNY157,708m and reaches CNY236,667m, requiring overseas revenue growth to become profitable local demand; overseas revenue rose from CNY221,884.773m to CNY310,740.988m.

blocks.heading: How much cash does BYD really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending reached RMB156,807.853 million. Free cash flow was negative RMB101,980.807 million after that investment, and “real free cash flow” was negative RMB102,892.788 million after treating stock compensation as an economic cost. BYD does not report that last subtotal; stock pay transfers value through ownership rather than using current cash.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for BYD today?

paragraphs.text: P/E means share price divided by forecast profit per share. dividend.opening: BYD paid RMB0.36 per share in 2025, down from RMB1.32 in 2024. In 2025, BYD's free cash flow was negative RMB101,980.807 million while it paid shareholders RMB16,062.454 million, so cash did not cover the payout.
dividend.closing: The full memo also answers questions about BYD's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does BYD pay per share?

paragraphs.text: BYD Auto Finance Company Limited is accounted for through equity accounting, so its customer loans and funding liabilities sit outside the consolidated balance sheet. Its earnings still matter, because they affect the group without showing every underlying asset and liability. Dividend restraint also signals caution: the 2025 dividend was RMB0.36 per share versus RMB1.32 in 2024.

blocks.heading: Does BYD's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: The break came in 2025. Free cash flow was negative RMB101,980.807 million, yet BYD paid shareholders RMB16,062.454 million. It raised RMB40,074.768 million from new shares and issued RMB154,003.870 million of debt. Cash still fell by RMB33,861.345 million, showing that expansion and distributions depended on financing and accumulated liquidity.

paragraphs.text: Dividends recover cautiously. The base path rises from CNY0.55 to CNY0.75, then reaches CNY0.95. The bear path holds at CNY0.36 initially before cutting to CNY0.20, while the bull path begins at CNY0.70 and reaches CNY1.40. The latest actual DPS was CNY0.36 after a prior peak of CNY1.32. Negative free cash flow of CNY101,980.807m supports restraint.

The view would move toward the bear case during 2027-2029 if price cuts reduce automotive margins, dealer inventory rises, or shipments outpace customer registrations. Slow overseas plant utilization would raise capital spending and debt while weakening free cash flow.

earnings.title: BYD earnings: October 29, 2026
earnings.meta_description: BYD's next results are expected on October 29, 2026; watch whether vehicle sales become earnings and operating cash.
earnings.opening: BYD's next results are expected on October 29, 2026. Watch whether BYD turns vehicle sales into earnings and operating cash.
earnings.closing: The full BYD memo also covers BYD's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The commitment is 20,000 FLASH Charging stations in China by December 2026. The system combines a car battery with charging stations that use stationary energy storage. That storage can deliver a powerful burst without requiring the local grid to provide all the electricity at once. But the promise is useful only if drivers can find working stations, and if those stations can recharge their own storage between busy periods.

The plan includes urban installations and highway sites. Using existing charging locations may reduce the work of finding land, but BYD still has to supply equipment, install it and keep it operating. The network therefore requires more than a successful technology demonstration.

blocks.heading: Did BYD keep its vehicle sales promise?

paragraphs.text: Management’s sales target also needs to be judged against its first promise. BYD initially indicated 5.5 million vehicle sales for 2025, then lowered the target to 4.6 million. Actual sales were 4,602,436, so the company met the revised goal but missed the original one.

blocks.heading: What do BYD's recent results show?

paragraphs.text: Q2 2026 earned more profit from less revenue, but the first half remained weaker than the previous year.

Revenue was RMB194,590.107 million, down 3.2%. Parent profit rose 29.7% to RMB8,240.857 million, while gross margin improved from 16.3% to 18.9%. That combination suggests better mix or economics, especially in overseas vehicles.
